storyboard.claim: Saying yes to a favor you dreaded.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman uneasy, phone in hand, while the friend with the paint roller waits for the yes.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the people living this claim.

storyboard.claim: A yes withdraws from a finite account of time and energy.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman holds an open wallet, uneasy, as if paying out.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the people living this claim.

storyboard.claim: The yes spends a finite amount of your time and energy.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An hourglass beside a slumped listener: finite time running out.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Extends the withdrawal metaphor to time and energy.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: the hourglass reads as time passing, the energy part is only in the callout.

storyboard.claim: People pleasing is an accounting problem, not a trait.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman pointing away, dismissing the trait label with a skeptical smirk.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The hosts now reframe the habit.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the people living this claim.

storyboard.claim: The habit is a financial leak we must stop.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Host talking directly to camera; the leak is carried by the callout.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: a leak has no literal icon, so only the callout carries it.

storyboard.claim: The episode draws on Damon Zahariades' book and psychology research.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A book icon with the host speaking, naming the author.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Introduces the source the hosts are using.
storyboard.addedInformation: Corrects the ASR spelling of the author's name to the proper form.

storyboard.claim: The book is The Art of Saying No.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Host holding a book.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Names the book introduced in the previous beat.
storyboard.addedInformation: Gives the exact title on screen.

storyboard.claim: The whole book rests on one sharp thesis.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Host pointing at the audience, as if about to state the thesis.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Leads into the thesis of the book.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: a pointing host carries little beyond the callout.

storyboard.claim: A no protects the yeses you actually mean.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A shield icon: a no guards the meaningful yeses.
storyboard.addedInformation: The shield makes protection literal, which is the claim.

storyboard.claim: Daily pressure on time is immense and growing.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A clock icon and a slumped listener: time pressure fills the day.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves from the thesis to the everyday pressure.
storyboard.addedInformation: The clock reads as time and deadlines, matching the calendar call.

storyboard.claim: A colleague's five-minute request always takes far longer.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The boss pointing at a document, dropping a task on the listener.
storyboard.addedInformation: The boss is the colleague who drops the request, so the cast matches the sentence.

storyboard.claim: Requests from friends, neighbours and groups keep coming in.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A phone icon with the friend asking for a favour.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Adds the friend and group-chat requests to the example.
storyboard.addedInformation: The phone reads as a modern message stream.

storyboard.claim: Agreeing to every demand has a staggering cost.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Boss dropping a task on the slumped, burdened Everyman.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the people living this claim.

storyboard.claim: Prioritizing others' requests shelves your own pursuits.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman reaches toward a book he wants to read while the friend's request pulls his attention away.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains the cost in concrete terms.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the people living this claim.

storyboard.claim: The downward spiral begins with exhaustion.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman slumped on the floor, eyes shut, spent.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Begins the spiral the narrator describes.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the people living this claim.

callout.text: Wear and tear on your body

storyboard.claim: Chronic stress wears the body down.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman hunched with a cup, drawn and strained.
storyboard.onScreenText: WEAR AND TEAR ON YOUR BODY
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the people living this claim.

storyboard.claim: Resentment toward yourself and the people you help.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman glaring while the neighbor cheerfully waits for more help.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Final stage of the spiral: resentment.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the people living this claim.

storyboard.claim: The yes happens before we even realize it.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman startled, looking at his emptied wallet.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Returns to the withdrawal metaphor to ask why.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the people living this claim.

storyboard.claim: Exhausted Tuesday evening, staring at the wall.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman lying flat, blank-faced, drained.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the people living this claim.

storyboard.claim: A friend's text asks you to help paint their living room this weekend.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Phone icon with the friend holding a paint roller asking for help.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The phone buzzes with the request.
storyboard.addedInformation: The friend's paint roller makes the favour concrete.

storyboard.claim: He texts yes before processing the dread.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A phone icon beside Everyman whose thumbs are already typing.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the people living this claim.

storyboard.claim: Sending the yes, the body sags at once.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman slumped, phone hanging limp.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the people living this claim.

storyboard.claim: The yes lands as the weight of a lost weekend.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman sagging as the friend cheerfully walks off with the paint roller.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the people living this claim.

storyboard.claim: The instant yes is a wired reflex, not generosity.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman jolts, already reaching for the buzzing phone.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the people living this claim.

storyboard.claim: Historically, saying no to the tribe meant exile, and exile meant death.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A door icon as exclusion, with a frightened listener.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains the evolutionary root of the reflex.
storyboard.addedInformation: The door reads as being shut out of the group.

storyboard.claim: The brain flags the request as a social threat.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman afraid, shrinking from the boss's demanding glare.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Modern brain version of the exile fear.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the people living this claim.

storyboard.claim: You text sure for dopamine relief, not the painting.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman texting sure, tense and relieved at once, not eager.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the people living this claim.

storyboard.claim: Years of training tie yes to short-term social survival.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman nervously smiling at the friend, relieved to escape the awkwardness.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the people living this claim.

storyboard.claim: The book gives a grounded example from the author's own college years.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Host holding the book, pointing to the example.
storyboard.addedInformation: Frames the anecdote as coming from the book.

callout.text: THE GUY WITH A PICKUP TRUCK

storyboard.claim: The author was the friend everyone asked to help them move.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A friendly young man as the person everyone asks for help.
storyboard.onScreenText: THE GUY WITH A PICKUP TRUCK
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: the pickup truck is not drawn; the callout names it.

storyboard.claim: He said yes to every request, like giving away a present.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A gift icon read as a yes handed away.
storyboard.addedInformation: The gift icon makes the giving-away of yeses literal.

storyboard.claim: He sacrificed studying, downtime and social life.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman lets his book go while the friend leads him away.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows the cost of the example.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the people living this claim.

storyboard.claim: Resentment and self-loathing, yet he could not stop saying yes.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman seething, slumped, as the friend asks yet again.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the people living this claim.

storyboard.claim: The hosts will challenge the evolutionary explanation.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Host pointing, starting a challenge.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Pivot from the example to a counter-argument.
storyboard.addedInformation: Signals the turn in the discussion.

storyboard.claim: Reducing everything to reflexes may ignore true altruism.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Host talking, posing the objection.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The objection to the evolutionary view.
storyboard.addedInformation: Frames the objection as a question for the audience.

storyboard.claim: Helping friends can be genuine warmth when you value the relationship.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A heart icon and a warm listener: real affection for friends.
storyboard.addedInformation: The heart reads as affection, matching the genuine-warmth case.

storyboard.claim: A supportive friend is different from an approval addict.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Host talking, with the approval addict label struck through.
storyboard.addedInformation: The strike rejects the label as the healthy alternative.

storyboard.claim: The book separates conscious generosity from reflexive pleasing.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A two-bucket sorter: conscious generosity on one side, reflexive pleasing on the other.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The structural distinction the episode turns on.
storyboard.addedInformation: Makes the two categories visible side by side.

storyboard.claim: A conscious yes is an investment when you have the bandwidth.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman pausing to weigh the request, relaxed and warm toward the friend.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the people living this claim.

storyboard.claim: Instinctive yes is the problem.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman answers the phone on reflex, anxious.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Contrast to the conscious path in the previous beat.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the people living this claim.
